failures.title: Mercedes M271.951/952 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing Chain Stretch and Camshaft Adjuster Wear
items.whatHappens: The M271 architecture is notorious for premature timing chain stretch and camshaft adjuster (VVT pulley) wear. This manifests as a distinct metallic rattling noise on cold starts, followed by check engine lights indicating camshaft correlation faults (e.g., P0016/P0017) and rough running. If ignored, the chain can jump teeth, causing catastrophic valve-to-piston contact.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, a full timing chain kit, tensioner, and updated camshaft adjuster replacement is viable. However, if the chain has already jumped and caused internal damage, a full Mercedes M271.951/952 engine replacement is the only reliable solution.

items.title: Direct Injection Carbon Buildup (CGI Specific)
items.whatHappens: Because fuel is injected directly into the cylinder rather than the intake port, there is no fuel "washing" effect to clean the intake valves. Oil vapours from the PCV system and EGR gases accumulate, forming hard carbon deposits on the intake valves and ports. This leads to rough idle, misfires, and reduced power.
items.repairVsReplace: Carbon buildup is addressed via walnut blasting or chemical cleaning of the intake tract, not engine replacement. However, severe neglect combined with timing chain issues can compound repair costs, making a reconditioned swap more economical than piecemeal repairs.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Mercedes M271.951/952
variants.intro: The M271.951 and M271.952 engine codes are stamped directly onto a machined pad on the engine block, typically located near the oil filter housing or the bell housing. The code is also clearly listed on your vehicle's V5C registration document under "Engine Number" and can be decoded from the full VIN. Common Confusion Warning: Owners frequently confuse the M271.951/952 with the pre-facelift M271.950 (156hp) and M271.960 (184hp), or the larger M274. While they share the same 1.8-litre turbocharged architecture, the .951/.952 variants feature revised ECU mapping and updated camshaft adjusters. Fitting a .950 or .960 as a direct replacement will result in ECU incompatibility and potential sensor mismatches. Furthermore, the M274 is a completely different 2.0-litre longitudinal engine with different accessory brackets, mounting points, and wiring looms, making it a non-starter for a direct swap.

relatives.description: - The pre-facelift CGI variants; owners of pre-2011 W204 or W212 models should look here, as the .951/.952 revisions feature updated camshaft adjusters and revised ECU mapping.

- The direct successor introduced from 2012, moving to a 2.0L turbocharged layout with significantly improved timing chain and camshaft adjuster designs, largely resolving the M271's most costly failure.

- The supercharged Kompressor variants of the same family; owners of pre-2007 W203 or W209 models should look here instead, as the port-injected architecture differs entirely from the CGI direct-injection setup.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement Mercedes M271.951/952 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Mercedes M271.951/952 is only advisable for lower-mileage host vehicles and *only* if accompanied by documented, stamped service history proving the timing chain, tensioner, and camshaft adjusters have been replaced. Without this history, the risk of inheriting the same catastrophic stretch issues is unacceptably high.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: This is the most recommended route for the M271.951/952. A proper reconditioned unit will include a brand-new timing chain kit, updated camshaft adjusters, and a cleaned intake tract to address CGI carbon buildup, directly addressing the engine's known weak points out of the box.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified if your original M271.951/952 suffered a jumped timing chain that damaged the cylinder head, valves, or pistons. A specialist rebuild will machine the block, fit updated timing components, and ensure all oil galleries are clear of debris from the failed chain.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing a replacement is only half the job. Our network provides full supply and fit services, ensuring the engine is installed by Mercedes-specialist technicians with a nationwide warranty backing both the labour and the unit.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: For facelift hosts like the W204 C-Class or W212 E-Class, current UK market values typically sit between £4,000 and £12,000 . With a reconditioned M271.951/952 replacement costing from £2,500 (plus fitting), the repair cost can represent 40-70% of the vehicle's value on well-kept examples, making replacement financially viable. However, on sub-£4,000 hosts, we strongly advise evaluating the car's scrap or part-exchange value before committing to a full engine replacement.

items.question: What is the most common failure with the Mercedes M271.951/952 engine?
items.answer: The most documented failure pattern for the M271.951/952 is timing chain stretch and camshaft adjuster wear, typically occurring between 60,000 and 100,000 miles. Early warning signs include a metallic rattling noise on cold starts and check engine lights for camshaft correlation faults, and as a CGI engine, intake valve carbon buildup is also a common secondary issue. Get quotes for a rebuilt M271.951/952 with the timing chain failure already addressed.

items.question: Which Mercedes models use the M271.951/952 engine?
items.answer: The M271.951 and M271.952 are fitted specifically to the facelift Mercedes-Benz C-Class (W204) and E-Class (W212) models from 2011 to 2014. They power badges including the C180 CGI, C200 CGI, C250 CGI, E200 CGI, and E250 CGI, and you should always verify your exact fitment via registration lookup. Confirm your exact M271.951/952 fitment before requesting a quote.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned Mercedes M271.951/952 engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned Mercedes M271.951/952 is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the well-documented timing chain stretch and camshaft adjuster failure risks. Used units carry a high probability of inheriting the same latent chain wear unless accompanied by stamped proof of a full chain kit replacement, whereas a proper reconditioned M271.951/952 includes a new timing chain, tensioner, and updated camshaft adjusters as standard. View our reconditioned Mercedes M271.951/952 engine options with 12-month warranties.

items.question: What is the difference between the M271.951/952 and the M271.950/960?
items.answer: The M271.951 and M271.952 are the updated 2011+ facelift revisions of the M271 CGI engine, featuring revised ECU mapping and updated camshaft adjuster components compared to the pre-2011 M271.950 and M271.960. While they share the same 1.8-litre turbocharged architecture, fitting a pre-facelift unit as a direct replacement can result in ECU incompatibility and potential sensor mismatches.
